subject: general
question: If a number is rational, it cannot be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rational and Irrational numbers are **mutually exclusive** sets.

A number can either be expressed as a fraction p/q (Rational) or it cannot (Irrational).

Natural numbers, Whole numbers, and Integers are all **subsets** of Rational numbers.

Since a number cannot belong to both sets simultaneously, a rational number can never be irrational.

**∴ The correct answer is Irrational.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A number is rational.

**Definition:** A rational number is any number that can be written in the form p/q, where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f73e7e8ead91b0dde2dd850338ab651e6b36476d8db7081773b142cf8223e1a.png] 

⇒ **Natural numbers** (1, 2, 3...) can be written as 1/1, 2/1, 3/1 (Rational).

⇒ **Whole numbers** (0, 1, 2...) can be written as 0/1, 1/1, 2/1 (Rational).

⇒ **Integers** (...−2, −1, 0, 1, 2...) can be written as −2/1, −1/1 (Rational).

⇒ **Irrational numbers** are those that cannot be expressed as p/q (e.g., √2, π).

⇒ If a number is in the Rational set, it is physically impossible for it to be in the Irrational set.

**∴ The correct answer is Irrational.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Real Number System

Real numbers are divided into two distinct groups: Rational and Irrational. Their intersection is an empty set.

Decimal Representation

Rational numbers have decimals that either **terminate** (e.g., 0.5) or **repeat** (e.g., 0.333...). Irrational numbers have **non-terminating** and **non-repeating** decimals.

Subsets of Rational Numbers

The hierarchy is: Natural Numbers ⊂ Whole Numbers ⊂ Integers ⊂ Rational Numbers.</p
